why: issue 2000 — how many passes a log dispatcher makes over `nros_log::early`'s held records before it releases the dispatch guard. A record that finds another delivery in progress (another thread, or a sink that logs) is held rather than dropped, and the holder delivers it; this bound is what keeps a sink that logs on every write from looping. Public so a test or a sizing note can state the bound instead of copying the number. rclrs/rcutils have no correspondent: rcutils hands each record to its output handler synchronously and keeps no queue.
